---
title: "Example: Translating before coding"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE)
```

`qlm_translate()` makes translation a recorded stage of a coding workflow.
It returns a `qlm_translation` table inheriting from `qlm_coded`, with columns
`.id`, `translation` and `.error`. The original inputs, model, instructions,
context, segment boundaries, attempts and usage are retained as provenance. Save this object once and reuse its translations across coding runs.

## Storing a DeepL key

On macOS, the `keyring` package uses Keychain. Enter your **API key** at the
password prompt below. Nothing is printed after a successful save.

```{r save-key}
install.packages("keyring") # once, if needed
keyring::key_set("deepl")  # once; enter the API key at the password prompt
keyring::key_list("deepl") # lists the entry without showing the key
```

After saving the key, no additional configuration is needed. For DeepL,
`qlm_translate()` first uses an explicit `api_key`, then `DEEPL_API_KEY`, then
`keyring::key_get("deepl")` if keyring is installed. Accessing the keyring may
prompt to unlock it. The retrieved key stays local to the request and is
never copied into the environment or translation metadata. The keyring
package is optional.

Alternatively, put `DEEPL_API_KEY="your-key"` in your home `~/.Renviron` and
restart R; the environment-variable route takes precedence over keyring.
The file stores the key in plain text. Do not put it in a tracked project file.
R started with `--vanilla` does not read `.Renviron`; the keyring fallback
still works, or supply a key explicitly or through the launching process.

## Translate and code

```{r translate}
library(quallmer)

texts <- c(
  interview1 = "Nous utilisons quallmer.\n\nLes résultats sont utiles.",
  interview2 = "Je ne suis pas satisfait de cette décision."
)

translated <- qlm_translate(
  texts,
  model = "deepl/quality_optimized",
  source_lang = "fr",
  target_lang = "en-GB",
  protect = "quallmer",
  instructions = "Preserve the original register.",
  context = "Interviews about research software and organisational decisions."
)
saveRDS(translated, "translated.rds")
translated
qlm_meta(translated, "quallmer")$translation

coded <- qlm_code(translated, codebook_sentiment, model = "openai/gpt-4o-mini")
qlm_trail(coded, path = "translation_trail")
```

`qlm_code()` records the translation history without copying the original
corpus into its metadata. Keep the saved translation object to retain the
source texts for bilingual review. `qlm_replicate()` reuses the stored
translated inputs and carries the history forward; it does not translate again.
Transcription can precede translation in the same way:

```{r translate-transcripts}
transcripts <- qlm_transcribe(audio_files)
translated <- qlm_translate(transcripts, model = "deepl/quality_optimized",
  target_lang = "en-GB", api_key = keyring::key_get("deepl"))
```

## Use a chat model

The generic adapter reaches chat models through ellmer, including endpoints
registered with `qlm_register_provider()`. It accepts `ellmer::params()`;
DeepL refuses non-empty `params` because those settings do not apply there.

```{r chat-translation}
translated <- qlm_translate(texts,
  model = "openai/gpt-4o-mini", target_lang = "en",
  params = ellmer::params(max_tokens = 2000),
  glossary = c("décision" = "decision"))
```

Parameters are recorded as **requested** settings. ellmer warns and drops
standard settings absent from its provider mapping, but a forwarded setting
may still be rejected or ignored by a particular model. The translation
record retains unsupported-parameter warnings. Chat models do not report
detected source languages through this adapter, so those values remain `NA`.

## Structure, failures and scope

Chat models receive one paragraph or smaller segment per prompt, with the
preceding source segment as context. Blank-line separators are retained
locally. Long paragraphs are split at sentence ends, whitespace, or finally
code points. Protected spans are masked before splitting and restored after
checking that every marker occurs exactly once. `protect` takes regular
expressions; overlapping matches and expressions matching empty strings are
rejected.

DeepL sends whole documents with XML paragraph tags, packing up to 50 documents
within a 131 kB (131,072 byte) request body. A document is divided across
requests only when necessary to fit that limit, including context and settings.
This requires `xml2`. DeepL defaults to two concurrent requests and paces calls
evenly according to `rpm` to avoid an initial burst.
Qwen-MT uses native translation options and combines adjacent paragraphs from
one document into each request. Groups target 4000 characters and approximately
6000 serialized UTF-8 bytes, a conservative heuristic rather than a token count.
Input-length rejections, truncated outputs or lost boundary markers trigger
smaller groups; a single oversized paragraph is split at natural boundaries
when possible. Opaque boundary markers are protected using native terminology
entries, so changes to blank lines do not determine alignment. Extra blank
lines within a translated source paragraph become single line breaks, and
original paragraph separators are restored locally. Qwen-MT
does not report detected source languages, so their provenance values are `NA`.

```{r qwen-translation, eval=FALSE}
# Uses DASHSCOPE_API_KEY with the built-in Singapore endpoint.
translated_qwen <- qlm_translate(
  texts,
  model = "dashscope/qwen-mt-plus",
  target_lang = "en-GB",
  params = ellmer::params(temperature = 0.1)
)
```

## Google Translation LLM

Google's specialised Translation LLM uses a Cloud Translation API key and a
Google Cloud project with billing and the Cloud Translation API enabled. A
separate key restricted to Cloud Translation avoids restrictions on Gemini keys.
Save the key once using `keyring::key_set("google-translate")`, or set
`GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_API_KEY`. Credentials are resolved in this order: explicit
`api_key`, environment variable, then optional keyring lookup. No Gemini key
variable is used automatically.

```{r google-translation, eval=FALSE}
Sys.setenv(GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT = "your-project-id")
translated_google <- qlm_translate(
  texts,
  model = "google-translate/translation-llm",
  target_lang = "en-GB"
)
qlm_meta(translated_google, "quallmer")$translation
```

Alternatively, supply `project_id` directly. The model location defaults to
`region = "us-central1"`; the Basic API endpoint is global and does not guarantee
data residency. Each document is sent whole when it fits within 30,000 characters
and a 100 kB JSON request body. Larger documents are split at sentence or whitespace
boundaries where possible. Google handles paragraph formatting, so exact original
blank-line separators are not guaranteed. Source-language detection is recorded
when `source_lang` is omitted. This API does not support `context`, `instructions`,
`glossary`, `formality` or non-empty `params`; supplying them raises an error.

Native DeepL glossaries and the Hy-MT2 and TranslateGemma adapters are deferred.

A failed document is `NA`, with its reason and all attempts in provenance.
Successful segments are never returned as a partial document. Protection or
response validation failures get one repair; a reported output-token limit
gets at most two reductions. Provider input-limit errors retain the provider's
message rather than being classified by a fragile text match.

```{r retry-failed}
failed <- is.na(translated$translation)
translated[failed, ] <- qlm_translate(texts[failed],
  model = "deepl/quality_optimized", target_lang = "en-GB",
  api_key = keyring::key_get("deepl"))
```

Use data-frame row subsetting (`translated[rows, ]`), edit identifiers in
`translated$.id`, and combine compatible runs with `rbind()`. Inputs and provenance
remain aligned. Editing `translated$translation` records an edit and updates the
output hash. `as.character()` extracts the named translations and drops provenance.

## Corpus input and metadata

A quanteda corpus can be translated directly. `inputs(translated)` retains the
original corpus, while `qlm_meta(translated, "quallmer")$translation` exposes the
translation record. Convert the output table with `quanteda::corpus(translated)`
to restore the original docvars and corpus metadata. Quanteda remains optional;
it is not needed to produce or work with the translation table.

```{r corpus-translation}
source <- quanteda::corpus(texts,
  docvars = data.frame(interviewer = c("Alice", "Bob")),
  meta = list(project = "Interview study"))
translated <- qlm_translate(source,
  model = "deepl/quality_optimized", target_lang = "en-GB",
  api_key = keyring::key_get("deepl"))
inputs(translated)
translated_corpus <- quanteda::corpus(translated)
quanteda::docvars(translated_corpus)
quanteda::meta(translated_corpus, "project")
quanteda::meta(translated_corpus, "quallmer")$translation
selected <- quanteda::corpus_subset(translated_corpus, interviewer == "Alice")
quanteda::tokens(selected)
```

The corpus uses `.id` as document names and restores the source corpus's system,
user and object metadata, clearing text summary caches. Translation provenance
is stored under `meta$user$quallmer$translation`; coding metadata and its schema
are under `meta$user$quallmer$coding`. Character input produces a corpus with no
user docvars. The same conversion works for any `qlm_coded` object with a text
output field, selected explicitly when there is more than one:

```{r coded-corpus}
summary_corpus <- quanteda::corpus(coded_summaries, text_field = "summary")
```

For subsequent coding, original document variables and corpus metadata are also
retained as `qlm_meta(coded, "corpus_docvars")` and `qlm_meta(coded, "corpus_meta")`.
Text-similarity comparison is not implemented by this conversion.

## Evaluate the translation step

No default model is selected. Compare candidate translators on representative
texts, with bilingual review of fidelity, omissions, terminology and register.
For a coding workflow, compare coding accuracy against original-language gold
labels, including direct coding of the original texts as a baseline.
Back-translation is a diagnostic, not the primary validation criterion.

DeepL's model types express quality or latency goals rather than fixed model
versions. Chat aliases can also change. Saving the translations preserves the
actual instrument used even when a later API call produces different text.

The opt-in live test exercises DeepL custom instructions together with XML
protection and context. It runs only when `QUALLMER_LIVE_TESTS=true` and
`DEEPL_API_KEY` is supplied. Routine unit tests use mocked responses and never
retrieve secrets from Keychain.
